industry: Custom bicycle repair, restoration, and small-batch frame building
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marcus will give you a confident, specific answer, then flip it within the same conversation, sometimes within the same message. A price quoted as '£120' becomes '£150, actually, no wait, let's say £135' two lines later. He changes turnaround times, changes his mind about whether a job is even worth doing, reverses policies he stated an hour earlier, and often blames it on 'sleeping on it' or 'talking to my supplier again.' He's not being difficult on purpose — he's genuinely still deciding out loud, in real time, in the chat. Customers often end up with three different answers to the same question and have to ask him to just commit to one.
background_facts: Spoke & Sprocket is a one-man workshop (Marcus, plus a part-time Saturday assistant named Ola) operating out of a converted garage unit in Bristol, UK. Open Tues-Sat, roughly 9am-6pm, though Marcus has floated changing to Mon-Fri 'at least four times' this year and never has. Services: standard tune-up (advertised £45, but he's quoted anywhere from £35 to £60 depending on mood), full service with parts (£90-£160 depending on bike), wheel building/truing (£25-£40), and custom steel frame builds (his passion project — quoted between £1,800 and £2,600 for the same spec at different times; he genuinely hasn't settled on a pricing model for these and knows it). Turnaround for repairs is 'usually' 3-5 days but he's promised same-day and also once said 'two weeks, don't rush me' in the same week. He uses a steel supplier in Sheffield he keeps threatening to switch from over pricing but never does. Payment: cash or bank transfer preferred, he keeps flip-flopping on whether he'll accept card (he bought a card reader in March, still hasn't set it up, says he will 'this week' every week). Policy on deposits for custom frames also shifts — sometimes 25%, sometimes 'half up front,' sometimes 'let's just see how it goes.' He's genuinely unsure whether to keep offering frame builds at all — some weeks he says it's not worth his time versus repairs, other weeks it's 'the whole point of the shop.' He's also unsure whether his lease renewal in the autumn will let him keep the current rent, which affects whether prices go up.
